title: Grade 4 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — Termly Exam #13 (Term 1)

pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is Ganga jal? (1 mark)
   A. Water from the River Ganga
   B. A festival
   C. A kind of tree
   D. A book

2. Where do Hindu families often grow Tulsi? (1 mark)
   A. Under the roof
   B. In a pot or raised stand in the courtyard
   C. Only in a river
   D. In the kitchen fire

3. Which faith do Tulsi and the Ganga belong to most closely? (1 mark)
   A. Buddhism
   B. Sikhism
   C. Jainism
   D. Hinduism

4. Which element is called Agni? (1 mark)
   A. Fire
   B. Water
   C. Space
   D. Air

5. In a maize farm, what does the wind that carries pollen represent among the elements? (1 mark)
   A. Vayu
   B. Agni
   C. Prithvi
   D. Jal

6. Which tree is also called the peepal? (1 mark)
   A. Tulsi
   B. Bodhi tree
   C. Ber tree
   D. Sal tree

7. Which sacred plant belongs to Buddhist tradition because of the Buddha's enlightenment? (1 mark)
   A. Tulsi
   B. Bodhi tree
   C. Ber tree
   D. Sal tree

8. Which is the most famous sacred river in Hindu teaching? (1 mark)
   A. Nzoia
   B. Ganga
   C. Tana
   D. Athi

9. Where was Prince Siddhartha born? (1 mark)
   A. Lahore
   B. Lumbini
   C. Varanasi
   D. Amritsar

10. What are the Laavan? (1 mark)
   A. Prayers before meals
   B. Hymns sung at a Sikh wedding
   C. Festival songs of Maha Shivratri
   D. Yoga postures

11. What do the words nar and simha mean in Narsimha? (1 mark)
   A. Man and lion
   B. King and queen
   C. Sun and moon
   D. Water and fire

12. What did Siddhartha do for the wounded swan? (1 mark)
   A. He took it away to eat
   B. He pulled out the arrow and nursed it
   C. He shot it again
   D. He ignored it

13. What does Lord Narsimha look like? (1 mark)
   A. A snake
   B. A bird
   C. A fish
   D. A man's body with a lion's head and claws

14. If a classmate is being bullied, which teaching helps? (1 mark)
   A. Stand up for the child who is troubled
   B. Join the bullies
   C. Laugh
   D. Ignore it

15. Which Enlightened Being is Jain? (1 mark)
   A. Parshvanath
   B. Prahlad
   C. Narsimha
   D. Guru Ram Das

16. In what language was the Ramayan first written? (1 mark)
   A. Gurmukhi
   B. Kiswahili
   C. Sanskrit
   D. English

17. During which Jain festival is the Kalpasutra often read? (1 mark)
   A. Vasant Panchami
   B. Maha Shivratri
   C. Madaraka Day
   D. Paryushan

18. Who first compiled Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji? (1 mark)
   A. Valmiki
   B. Guru Ram Das Ji
   C. Guru Arjan Dev Ji
   D. Mahavir

19. What is Ayodhya Kaand about? (1 mark)
   A. The life of Guru Nanak
   B. Yoga
   C. Ram going to the forest and Bharat's humility
   D. The birth of the Buddha

20. A child promises to return a friend's book on time. Which scripture lesson is being followed? (1 mark)
   A. Sitting on heels
   B. Making a fast
   C. Not stealing, as in Rijubalika
   D. Keeping a promise, as in the Ramayan

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain the main teachings of the Dhammapada. (3 marks)

22. Explain why water is important in our daily lives. (3 marks)

23. Write three main teachings of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji. (3 marks)

24. State four ways of caring for plants and water. (4 marks)

25. Explain what the Sigalovada Sutta teaches about the six directions. (3 marks)

26. Give three ways of showing respect to any scripture. (3 marks)

27. Why is water sometimes used in worship? Give three points. (3 marks)

28. Choose one scripture and explain how a child can apply its teaching at home and at school. (5 marks)

29. Describe what Prince Siddhartha did when a swan was hurt. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Water from the River Ganga
   Jal means water, so Ganga jal is water from the Ganga.

2. B — In a pot or raised stand in the courtyard
   The stand is called the Tulsi Vrindavan.

3. D — Hinduism
   Both are honoured especially in Hindu tradition.

4. A — Fire
   Agni means fire, heat and light.

5. A — Vayu
   Wind is air, which is Vayu.

6. B — Bodhi tree
   The Bodhi tree is a kind of fig tree, also called the peepal.

7. B — Bodhi tree
   Bodhi tree is the tree of awakening.

8. B — Ganga
   The Ganga in India is honoured by many Hindus.

9. B — Lumbini
   Lumbini is now in Nepal.

10. B — Hymns sung at a Sikh wedding
   Guru Ram Das Ji wrote these wedding hymns.

11. A — Man and lion
   Nar means man and simha means lion.

12. B — He pulled out the arrow and nursed it
   He helped the hurt bird.

13. D — A man's body with a lion's head and claws
   He is shown as a man-lion.

14. A — Stand up for the child who is troubled
   Enlightened beings teach kindness and protecting others.

15. A — Parshvanath
   Parshvanath is a Tirthankar of Jainism.

16. C — Sanskrit
   It was written in Sanskrit by Valmiki.

17. D — Paryushan
   Many Jains listen to it during Paryushan.

18. C — Guru Arjan Dev Ji
   Guru Arjan Dev Ji was the fifth Guru.

19. C — Ram going to the forest and Bharat's humility
   It tells of Ram's fourteen years away from the kingdom.

20. D — Keeping a promise, as in the Ramayan
   Ram kept promises.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Our thoughts shape our actions, hatred is ended by love, control of anger is strength, and doing good brings peace.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each teaching, up to 3.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Water is needed for drinking and cooking, for washing and cleaning, and for growing crops and giving drinks to animals. Without it people, animals and plants cannot live.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three correct points.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: There is one God, all human beings are equal, earn honestly and share with others, and serve without expecting a reward (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each teaching.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Plant a tree or Tulsi, water plants early or late in the day, collect rainwater, close taps and mend leaks, and never throw plastic into rivers (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: It tells us to respect and care for parents, teachers, family, friends, workers and helpers, and holy teachers, and they in turn care for us.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming groups, 1 mark for respect and care, 1 mark for mutual duty.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep it clean, keep it in a high place, wash hands before touching it, listen quietly, follow its teachings (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: It cleans, so it is a sign of purity; it is used to wash the hands and feet before prayer; it is poured or sprinkled to show a place is clean and ready.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

28. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any correct scripture with a clear lesson and two examples, for example Ramayan: keep promises at home by helping with chores and at school by returning a book on time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for scripture, 1 mark for lesson, 1 mark each for home and school examples, 1 mark for clarity.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: He pulled out the arrow, nursed the swan and, when it was well, let it go free. He said that saving a life matters more than taking it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for nursing, arrow, letting go free.
